newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Kashmir guerrilla violence declining.
newsitem.headline: India says Kashmir guerrilla violence declining.

text.p: Indian authorities said on Sunday guerrilla violence in Kashmir had tapered off this year, but separatists denied the claim.

"There has been more than a 25 percent decline in incidents of militancy and killings in Jammu and Kashmir during the first four months of the current year," a state government statement quoted an official spokesman as saying.
He said 1,200 incidents were reported between January and April, down from 1,600 over the same period last year.
A total of 718 people were killed in violence related to the separatist campaign in the first four months, compared with 949 in the corresponding period, he said.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year-old rebellion against Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir, the mostly Hindu nation's only Moslem-majority state.
Kashmir's leading separatist alliance, the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, denied that violence was on the wane.
"We are not surprised with the false claims of the government," Hurriyat chairman Umar Farooq told Reuters.
"The fact is that the rate of killings and the number of violent incidents in the (Kashmir) valley has increased. There is a sharp increase in state terrorism."

Umar Farooq accused Indian security forces of killing at least 818 people in the first four months of this year, killing many others in custody and blowing up scores of houses belonging to relatives of suspected guerrillas.
"The real facts and figures reflect that there is no decline in separatism and state terrorism in Kashmir," Umar Farooq said.
More than a dozen guerrilla groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir.
